title: QBR: Bridgewater health + runway sprint
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-09-11 | Start: 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~58m | Recording: enabled | Location: Zoom
Notes: Q3 QBR focused on usage trends, cost spikes in August, reliability incidents, next 90d runway and a small capacity pilot (burst). Shared artifacts: deck (bit.ly/redwood-bw-q3), benchmark sheet (drive.google.com/dl/bridgewater-bench)
summary: Quarterly health check: usage up 42% month-over-month driven by new recommendation feature. Costs spiked due to longer context + higher concurrency in customer-facing workflows. Two brief reliability incidents in August (KV cache miss / autoscale lag). Customer wants a short pilot to validate Dedicated pools + autoscale tuning; finance asked for clearer unit economics and a projected 90-day burn. Agreed next steps: PRICING + POC SCOPE + TECH BENCHMARKS.
action_items: Maya Chen: Share tailored pricing model and 3-month cost projection (due 2025-09-15)
Diego Alvarez: Run latency/cost microbenchmarks using Bridgewater sample traces and share results (due 2025-09-18)
Sara Liu / Tom Reed: Provide 48h of raw request traces and a representative prompt set (due 2025-09-13)
Nina Park: Schedule kickoff for a 2-week Dedicated pilot and invite infra owners (due 2025-09-16)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing + pilot proposal
Customer to approve pilot scope and provide traces
Schedule technical bench run and follow-up demo week of 9/22
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, well get started. i'll do a quick frame then hand off to diego for the incident details.
[00:14] Sara Liu: thanks maya, appreciate it. quick note, priya's on for finance, tom for platform.
[00:18] Diego Alvarez: yeah hi folks, diego here. quick agenda recap: usage trends, incidents, options (hosted/dedicated/private) and pilot scope.
[00:34] Tom Reed: i want to call out the spike — we saw concurrency up 3x on weekdays and long sequences from the new summarize flow, so tokens exploded.
[00:49] Maya Chen: that matches what we saw in telemetry — 42% mo/mo increase. question for you, sara — is the long context mostly from user-session aggregation or from adding more context to each request?
[01:05] Sara Liu: it's a mix. customer sessions get enriched with more data, plus we added a 2k prompt for follow-ups. we didn't expect the cumulative kv cache effect.
[01:19] Diego Alvarez: hmm kv cache — that explains the miss pattern during the incidents. our logs show the cache miss rate jumped right before the autoscale lag.
[01:31] Tom Reed: autoscale lag, yeah. around 8/18 our autoscaler took like 70s to spin up extra instances.
[01:40] Diego Alvarez: right, we looked at queueing and saw a tail latency event. likely a combination of pod cold starts + long-running token streams.
[01:50] Priya Nair: from finance side, cost was the big alarm. we saw a 58% increase month spend in August. need a clear breakdown per model tier and per customer segment.
[02:03] Maya Chen: absolutely — we can send a model-by-model cost breakdown and unit economics. quick thought: moving heavier traffic to a quantized variant and enabling prefix caching should cut unit cost 20-30% depending on your latency SLO.
[02:19] Sara Liu: quantized variant — were sensitive about quality so need to see evals. can you show the delta on our prompt set?
[02:28] Diego Alvarez: yes, that's the plan — we will run diegos bench against your traces. quick aside, sometimes quantization degrades rare-token fidelity, but often fine for summarization. we'll instrument ROUGE/BLEU-ish and prompt-specific checks.
[02:45] Ethan Cole: (joined) sorry i'm late — quick context, we're looking at a Q4 launch if pilot goes well, timeline is tight.
[02:55] Maya Chen: welcome ethan. so timeline wise, pilot in Sept, evaluate in Oct, go/no-go early Nov consistent with a Q4 launch.
[03:08] Tom Reed: curious on Dedicated: is it mandatory to reserve for predictable throughput, or can we mix hosted for peak and dedicated baseline?
[03:20] Diego Alvarez: mixing is supported. common pattern: baseline on Dedicated pool to guarantee KV locality and lower tail latency, burst to hosted to absorb unexpected spikes. routing policies handle fallback and region preferences.
[03:33] Sara Liu: are there SLAs on failover and warmup? we can't have 60s cold starts in production.
[03:41] Maya Chen: dedicated has much lower cold-start risk — we can configure node warm pools and faster autoscale policies. we also have automatic fallback to a lighter model to keep error rates low during node issues.
[03:54] Priya Nair: what's the estimated cost delta if we go Dedicated baseline for 200 concurrency? need numbers.
[04:01] Maya Chen: we'll share a projection — ballpark, Dedicated gives ~25% lower per-token cost at steady state for heavy workloads, but there's a base commit to cover. well show scenario math in the spreadsheet.
[04:15] Tom Reed: security / compliance — we need SOC2 artifacts and SSO integration details for the pilot.
[04:22] Nina Park: got it — i'll attach SOC2 + SAML SSO steps in the follow-up doc. for private we can also do VPC peering if needed.
[04:34] Sara Liu: on incidents — can you summarize the root cause quick?
[04:38] Diego Alvarez: short version: three factors aligned: increased token volume, KV cache miss spikes due to session fragmentation, and autoscaler lag during the traffic crest. postmortem suggests tuning cache TTLs, pre-warming instances, and refining batch sizes.
[04:55] Sara Liu: did you see any model-level CPU saturation or is it infra?
[05:00] Diego Alvarez: mostly infra — kernel sched and a few pods hit VRAM pressure during peak; we recommend moving some large prompts to a higher-memory SKU in the short term.
[05:12] Priya Nair: finance asks for a worst-case 30-day burn if traffic doubles — can you model that?
[05:19] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include a worst-case scenario. we'll give three scenarios: conservative, expected, worst-case.
[05:27] Tom Reed: about instrumentation — can we get token-level cost mapping per route?
[05:32] Maya Chen: yes, console provides token-level breakdown by route and model. we'll also share sample dashboards and a lightweight JSON export for your cost deck.
[05:44] Sara Liu: for the pilot scope — two-week pilot, baseline dedicated pool sized for current qps, load test to 2x, latency/cost comparison, and run your benchmark on our prompt set.
[05:58] Diego Alvarez: sounds good. technical checklist: we need traces, sample prompts, SSO creds for test users, and a small dataset for evals.
[06:08] Ethan Cole: can you also include a rollback criteria? CTO wants clear exit conditions.
[06:13] Maya Chen: yes — rollback criteria: sustained 2x latency increase over baseline OR >10% degradation in P95 or more than 0.5% error rate increase during pilot. we'll write that in the pilot doc.
[06:26] Priya Nair: for finance, also want a committed price if we sign Dedicated for 6 months.
[06:32] Maya Chen: we can propose a 6-month reserved tier with stepped discounts; i'll include that in the pricing doc.
[06:40] Tom Reed: any required infra changes on our side?
[06:44] Diego Alvarez: minimal — peering and sample creds. if you want VPC private, well coordinate networking but pilot can run over secure peering.
[06:56] Sara Liu: ok, timeline recap?
[06:58] Maya Chen: action items as shared: traces by 9/13, pricing and pilot proposal by 9/15, bench results by 9/18. schedule pilot kickoff 9/22.
[07:12] Tom Reed: sounds good.
[07:15] Maya Chen: any other questions?
[07:17] Priya Nair: just to confirm, will we get a written SLA for the pilot?
[07:21] Nina Park: yes, we'll include a pilot SLA and the rollback criteria in the doc.
[07:28] Sara Liu: perfect. thanks team.
[07:31] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with the deck and pricing.
[07:34] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels (Ethan joined late and appears mid-transcript). Some technical terms may be transcribed imperfectly (kv cache sometimes as "kayvee cache").
